title: A paint spot on the nose, and knowing the reflection is you
summary: OpenStax says that around 18 months a toddler knows the mirror image is themselves, because children in a cited study touched a paint spot on their own nose.
body: OpenStax Psychology says infants do not have a self-concept, an understanding of who they are. A child in front of a mirror reaches toward the image as if it were another child. By about 18 months, the page says, a toddler recognizes that the person in the mirror is themselves. The evidence it describes is a study that put a red dot of paint on children's noses: at 18 months they touched their own noses when they saw the spot. By 24 to 36 months, the page says, children can name or point to themselves in pictures. The study named is Amsterdam, 1972, which was not opened here. Liking a mirror at 6 months, on a sheet checklist, is a different claim and does not say the child knows the reflection is theirs.
